title: Machine Unlearning in Gradient Boosting Decision Trees

problem.claim: Machine learning models may memorize training data, creating a need to unlearn user data requested for deletion.

gap.claim: Few studies investigate machine unlearning for Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, and methods developed for deep neural networks do not straightforwardly transfer to GBDT settings.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a GBDT unlearning framework that unlearns a given collection of data without retraining the model from scratch.
The framework uses random split point selection and random partitioning-layer training to reduce subtree retraining during unlearning.

The framework stores intermediate data and statistics to identify subtrees requiring retraining without accessing the original training dataset, and includes a lazy update technique to trade off unlearning time and model functionality.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first work to consider machine unlearning on GBDT.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors experimentally evaluated their methods on public datasets.
The authors report that the empirical results confirm the effectiveness of their framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data deletion requirements and potential model memorization motivate machine unlearning.
GBDTs are widely deployed, but their unlearning problem has received limited study and cannot be addressed by straightforwardly transferring DNN methods.
The paper formalizes machine unlearning and a relaxed version of the problem.
The authors present a framework and supporting training, storage, and lazy-update techniques for efficient GBDT unlearning.
The methods are evaluated on public datasets, with the authors reporting effective empirical results.

source_observation.claim: The framework is designed to reduce subtree retraining and avoid retraining the entire model from scratch.

interpretation.claim: Unlearning efficiency can be improved by structuring model training to localize future deletion-related updates.

application.claim: When designing deletion-capable tree ensembles, consider partitioning and stored intermediate statistics that support targeted updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach performs across datasets, deletion workloads, or model-functionality requirements.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definitions of the unlearning problem or its relaxed version.
The abstract does not report dataset identities, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not quantify the trade-off between unlearning time and model functionality.
